newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Von Roll says provisions in equity charge.
newsitem.headline: Von Roll says provisions in equity charge.

text.p: Swiss engineering group Von Roll Holding AG said provisions for potential damages in a legal dispute with steelmaker von Moos were included in 140 million Swiss francs taken out of equity in 1996.
Von Roll executives declined to say how much of the equity charge was for provisions and how much for other costs linked to the company's withdrawal from the steel business.

"Divestment costs for the steel business total 140 million Swiss francs, which includes depreciation of Von Roll Steel, provisions for the arbitration case and accumulated depreciation for New Jersey Steel Corporation," chief operating officer Georg Hanloser told a news conference on 1996 results.
Von Roll said earlier on Wednesday it had taken provisions for the legal row with von Moos but said nothing about the amount.
Chairman Max Amstutz said the company would not make public how high provisions were for the dispute over a Swiss steel plant sold last year to von Moos.

The Gerlafingen plant was part of Von Roll's overall Swiss steel business sold to von Moos last June as Von Roll sought to quit its traditional steel focus and concentrate on three core engineering areas that promised more stable profit growth.
But Von Moos said in September it was pulling out of the deal retroactively, based on its claims that the Gerlafingen plant did not live up to standards promised by Von Roll.
An arbitration court is now reviewing the dispute.
"The provisions contained in this charge of 140 million are based on a worst-case scenario, if the decision goes completely against Von Roll," Amstutz said.
"We hope the full amount will not be needed," he added.

Hahnloser said management believed the equity charge was enough to cover all expected costs from quitting the steel business, including depreciation at New Jersey Steel Corporation (NJSCO), based in Sayreville, New Jersey.

"Based on what we know about the arbitration case (with von Moos) and on what we know about developments at NJSCO, we are convinced that we have put aside sufficient provisions for both areas," Hahnloser said.
The third point covered by the equity charge was depreciation at Von Roll Steel, the division it sold to von Moos.
Von Roll's total equity at the end of 1996 fell to 458 million Swiss francs from 567 million a year earlier, mainly due to the 140 million charge.
